lessons.title: Memory Management Basics
lessons.content: Kotlin/JVM uses automatic garbage collection, but excessive short-lived object creation triggers more frequent GC pauses. Real scenario: avoiding new lambda allocation inside onBindViewHolder called thousands of times per scroll.

lessons.title: Inline Functions and Performance
lessons.content: inline eliminates lambda allocation and call overhead by copying the function body to the call site. Real scenario: stdlib's forEach/map on Arrays are inline, avoiding allocation overhead you'd expect from functional style.

codeSnippets.code: intArray.forEach { value -> process(value) } // compiles like a manual loop

lessons.title: Sequence vs Collection Performance
lessons.content: List operations are eager, creating full intermediate lists; Sequence is lazy, evaluated per-element. Real scenario: processing 100,000 items through 3 chained operations - Sequence avoids 2 unnecessary intermediate lists.

lessons.title: Choosing the Right Collection Type
lessons.content: Different implementations have different performance characteristics: List for indexed access, HashMap for O(1) lookup. Real scenario: choosing HashMap for a lookup-heavy cache instead of scanning a List.

codeSnippets.code: val userMap = userList.associateBy { it.id } // O(1) lookup instead of O(n) find

lessons.title: Boxing and Unboxing
lessons.content: Primitives stored unboxed when possible, but generic type arguments like List<Int> force boxing. Real scenario: preferring IntArray over List<Int> in performance-critical numeric loops.

codeSnippets.code:
val boxed: List<Int> = listOf(1, 2, 3)     // boxed Integer objects
val unboxed: IntArray = intArrayOf(1, 2, 3) // no boxing

lessons.title: Minimizing Unnecessary Object Allocation
lessons.content: Every allocation has a cost, contributing to GC pressure - prefer reusing objects in hot paths. Real scenario: hoisting a Regex object outside a loop instead of recreating it per iteration.

codeSnippets.code:
private val pattern = Regex("[a-z]+") // created once, reused
fun isValid(s: String) = s.matches(pattern)

lessons.title: General Performance Best Practices
lessons.content: Measure before optimizing, prefer val over var, avoid Sequence on small collections where its overhead outweighs benefits. Real scenario: reaching for Sequence on a 10-item list can actually be slower than plain List.

codeSnippets.code:
// small collection: plain List is typically faster
smallList.map { transform(it) }.filter { it.isValid }
